summary: Settlements stopped because order-service deployment dep-6010 (v2.16.0, rolled out 07:40:01Z) renamed the OrderExecuted field qty->quantity and set the event schema header to v2, while settlement-service's consumer still deserializes v1. The first v2 message (orders-3@8841207) failed at 07:42:14Z ('missing required field qty, schema v1 expected, header says v2'), was retried as a poison message, and blocked the partition. settlement._lag climbed from ~40 to 60,124 by 09:54 while request_rate fell to 0.4 req/s. The poll-record config change cfg-3004 (07:35, 500->200) is a coincidence/misattribution: a batch-size setting cannot cause a per-message schema deserialize failure, and the error began 2 minutes after the v2 deploy whose change notes name the exact renamed field. Kafka shows no rebalance and resources (DB pool flat, no restarts) rule out exhaustion. Fix: roll back dep-6010 or make settlement-service handle schema v2, then unblock/skip the poisoned offset.

ranked_hypotheses.title: order-service v2.16.0 schema change breaks settlement-service consumer
ranked_hypotheses.statement: Deployment dep-6010 (order-service v2.16.0, 07:40) renamed the OrderExecuted field qty->quantity and bumped the schema header to v2. settlement-service's consumer still parses v1, so the first v2 message (orders-3@8841207) fails to deserialize, is retried as a poison message, and blocks that partition. No settlements post, the partition stalls, and consumer lag grows unboundedly.

causal_chain.claim: dep-6010 renames qty->quantity and sets event schema header v2
settlement consumer expects v1 and fails to deserialize the v2 message
failed message is retried as a poison message and blocks the partition
partition blocked -> zero settlements processed, consumer_lag grows to 60k

assumptions: settlement-service has not been updated to handle OrderExecuted schema v2
no rollback of dep-6010 or schema-registry fix was applied before the data window ends

ranked_hypotheses.title: cfg-3004 poll-record reduction caused the stall
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The reported suspect: config change cfg-3004 (consumer.max.poll.records 500->200, 07:35) on settlement-service caused the consumer to stall and lag to grow.

causal_chain.claim: smaller poll batches change consumer throughput

assumptions: poll batch size could produce a hard per-message deserialize failure
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: The failure mode is a per-message schema deserialization error on a single message id (orders-3@8841207 'missing required field qty'), which poll batch size cannot cause. It also began 2 minutes after the v2 deployment whose change summary explicitly renames the missing field.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Kafka partition reassignment / broker issue stalled the consumer
ranked_hypotheses.statement: Infrastructure-level Kafka rebalance or partition loss (as in HIST-104/HIST-112) stalled settlement-service's consumer.

causal_chain.claim: consumer loses assignment and lag grows

assumptions: kafka rebalance occurred but was not logged
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: kafka logs show no rebalance/reassignment events (only two benign connection-reset retries), and the settlement errors are explicit schema v1-vs-v2 deserialization failures, not assignment loss.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Resource exhaustion on settlement-service
ranked_hypotheses.statement: CPU/memory/DB connections exhaustion caused settlement-service to stop consuming.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: DB pool flat at ~6 connections and no restarts; elevated CPU (~70%) is a consequence of busy-looping poison retries, and request_rate collapse is downstream of the blocked partition rather than a cause.

facts.statement: settlement-service first logged OrderExecuted deserialize failures at 07:42:14Z on orders-3@8841207 with 'missing required field qty (schema v1 expected, header says v2)', followed by poison-message retries marking the partition blocked.
order-service dep-6010 (v2.16.0) completed rollout at 07:40:01Z with changes renaming OrderExecuted field qty->quantity and adding schema header v2.
The only config change was cfg-3004 on settlement-service setting consumer.max.poll.records 500->200 at 07:35:00Z.
settlement-service consumer_lag grew from ~40 to 60124 and request_rate fell from ~62 req/s to 0.4 req/s.
settlement-service CPU rose to ~70% while DB pool stayed ~6 connections and restarts remained 0, and error_rate stayed flat at ~0.2%.
kafka logged no rebalance, only two benign connection-reset retries.
Historical similar incidents (HIST-104, HIST-112) were partition-reassignment causes, not schema mismatch.

assumptions: settlement-service has not been independently updated to parse OrderExecuted schema v2.
No rollback of dep-6010 or schema-registry migration was applied within the observed window (dep-6010 status is 'live', rolled_back_at is null).
The v2 messages are continuously produced by order-service, so the blocked partition cannot self-recover.

timeline.event: Config change cfg-3004 applied to settlement-service: consumer.max.poll.records 500->200 (reporter's suspected cause).
order-service deployment dep-6010 (v2.16.0) rollout complete: OrderExecuted qty renamed to quantity, schema header v2.
settlement-service first deserialize error on orders-3@8841207 (schema v1 expected, header says v2).
consumer_lag ~4167 and request_rate collapsed to 0.4 req/s; CPU elevated to ~70%.

recommended_actions.action: Roll back order-service dep-6010 to v2.15.x (or publish a v1-compatible OrderExecuted) to stop producing schema-v2 events.
recommended_actions.rationale: The v2 schema header and qty->quantity rename are the direct trigger of the deserialize failures.

recommended_actions.action: Make settlement-service tolerate schema v2 (accept 'quantity' as alias for 'qty') and skip/dead-letter the poisoned offset orders-3@8841207 to unblock the partition.
recommended_actions.rationale: The partition stays blocked on the poison message, so lag cannot drain until it is consumed or skipped.

recommended_actions.action: Add a schema-compatibility gate (consumer-driven contract / schema registry check) to the order-service release pipeline.
recommended_actions.rationale: A consumer-breaking field rename shipped with no compatibility check, causing a cross-service outage.

recommended_actions.action: Add alerting on consumer_lag growth and poison-message/partition-blocked errors rather than relying on HTTP 5xx.
recommended_actions.rationale: error_rate stayed flat at ~0.2% while lag grew to 60k, so existing signals did not page.

recommended_actions.action: Do not revert cfg-3004 as the primary mitigation (optionally revert for cleanliness); it is not the root cause.
recommended_actions.rationale: Poll batch size cannot cause a per-message schema deserialize failure.

data_gaps: No settlement-service logs were checked after 10:00Z to confirm whether lag eventually drained or a rollback/unblock occurred; later-window logs and metrics were not queried.
No schema-registry or order-service publish-side telemetry was available to confirm how many v2 messages were produced or whether a compatibility check exists.
Root-cause is inferred from the deployment change summary (qty->quantity + header v2) matching the consumer's error; the schema-registry diff itself was not directly observed.
The exact upstream message offset/consumer group configuration of orders-3@8841207 was not retrieved from kafka telemetry.
